title: Microtask State Dispatch Batcher
subtopicTitle: Automatic Batching in React 18 vs flushSync
problemStatement: Implement `createBatchingStore(initialState, onRender)` that batches multiple synchronous `setState` calls so that `onRender` fires only ONCE with the merged state at the end of the microtask turn.
interviewTrap: Before React 18, updates inside `fetch().then()` triggered 2 renders for 2 `setState` calls. React 18 batches them into 1 render.

testCases.name: Batches multiple synchronous state updates into 1 render call
testCases.testFn: let renders = 0; const store = createBatchingStore({ a: 1, b: 2 }, () => renders++); store.setState({ a: 10 }); store.setState({ b: 20 }); store.setState({ a: 30 }); await Promise.resolve(); return renders;

testCases.name: Applies all sequential updates to final state
testCases.input: final state reflects all batched changes
testCases.testFn: let finalState = null; const store = createBatchingStore({ a: 1, b: 2 }, s => { finalState = s; }); store.setState({ a: 10 }); store.setState({ b: 20 }); store.setState({ a: 30 }); await Promise.resolve(); return finalState;

testCases.name: Supports functional updaters during batching
testCases.testFn: let finalState = null; const store = createBatchingStore(0, s => { finalState = s; }); store.setState(p => p + 1); store.setState(p => p + 1); store.setState(p => p + 1); await Promise.resolve(); return finalState;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: In React 17, state updates inside `setTimeout` or `Promise.then` were NOT batched, triggering multiple re-renders. React 18 automatically batches ALL state updates regardless of origin. `flushSync(() => { ... })` opts out of batching, forcing an immediate synchronous DOM flush.

2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is State Batching in React and how does it prevent render thrashing?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Batching is when React groups multiple state updates (`setCount(c => c + 1); setFlag(f => !f);`) into a single re-render pass instead of re-rendering twice. This prevents intermediate inconsistent UI states and eliminates redundant DOM diffing.

realWorldUseCases.description: Resetting 10 form fields in a single event handler triggers exactly 1 re-render pass.

howToExplain.opening: Batching consolidates multiple state setter calls within an event turn into a single re-render pass, optimizing render performance.
keyPoints: Groups multiple setState calls into one render cycle.
Processes pending updates via an internal update queue.
A foundational optimization in all React versions.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Batching ensures component re-renders scale with user actions rather than the number of state variables.
analogies: Ordering at a restaurant: you tell the waiter your appetizer, entree, and drink together; the waiter makes one trip to the kitchen, not three.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming state updates immediately after calling setState: `setCount(1); console.log(count); // still 0`.
commonMistakes.why: State updates are asynchronous and batched; the variable in the current render closure remains unchanged until the next render pass.
commonMistakes.correct: State reflects new values only on the subsequent render pass.

followUpDeepDive.question: How did React 17 batch updates inside event handlers?
followUpDeepDive.answer: React 17 wrapped synthetic event handlers in `discreteUpdates()` which flushed updates at the end of the event handler callback.
